name: std::log(std::complex)
intro: Computes complex natural (base e) logarithm of a complex value z with a branch cut along the negative real axis.

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: If no errors occur, the complex natural logarithm of z is returned, in the range of a strip in the interval [−iπ, +iπ] along the imaginary axis and mathematically unbounded along the real axis.

sections.title: Error handling and special values
sections.text:
Errors are reported consistent with math_errhandling.

If the implementation supports IEEE floating-point arithmetic,

The function is continuous onto the branch cut taking into account the sign of imaginary part
 std::log(std::conj(z)) == std::conj(std::log(z))
 If z is (-0,+0), the result is (-∞,π) and FE_DIVBYZERO is raised
 If z is (+0,+0), the result is (-∞,+0) and FE_DIVBYZERO is raised
 If z is (x,+∞) (for any finite x), the result is (+∞,π/2)
 If z is (x,NaN) (for any finite x), the result is (NaN,NaN) and FE_INVALID may be raised
 If z is (-∞,y) (for any finite positive y), the result is (+∞,π)
 If z is (+∞,y) (for any finite positive y), the result is (+∞,+0)
 If z is (-∞,+∞), the result is (+∞,3π/4)
 If z is (+∞,+∞), the result is (+∞,π/4)
 If z is (±∞,NaN), the result is (+∞,NaN)
 If z is (NaN,y) (for any finite y), the result is (NaN,NaN) and FE_INVALID may be raised
 If z is (NaN,+∞), the result is (+∞,NaN)
 If z is (NaN,NaN), the result is (NaN,NaN)

sections.title: Notes
sections.text:
The natural logarithm of a complex number z with polar coordinate components (r,θ) equals ln r + i(θ+2nπ), with the principal value ln r + iθ.

The semantics of this function are intended to be consistent with the C function clog.
